subtype: Signing a tiny pledge, then being asked for more [Receiver]
passage: Kiran, before you sign up for more of those online challenges, hear your Baljeet Mama's story. At sixteen, I had just made my first email ID at the cyber café. A site asked me to sign an online pledge to "stand with farmers." One click. Easy. A week later they wrote, "As a pledger, will you donate fifty rupees?" Fifty rupees was my whole week's money, but how could a pledger say no? I paid. Then they asked me to get ten classmates to pay too, and to send my father's phone number for "updates." That's when my stomach turned. I told my father that same evening, and he asked, "Would you have given fifty rupees and my number to strangers on the first day?" No. Each yes had made the next one feel owed.

qa.a: When they asked for his father's phone number, he felt uneasy and told his father that evening, whose question showed he would never have agreed on the first day.

qa.a: He may have been concerned that strangers wanted his number and his son's classmates' money, but he helped calmly with a simple question.
